subject: Post-call: StreamlineAI cost & performance discovery — next steps
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.inference>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia@streamlineai.com>, Tom Baker <tbaker@streamlineai.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.inference>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-04-20T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: StreamlineAI cost & performance discovery — next steps

Thanks again for a productive call today — quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned. Short version: you have clear unit-economics pressure, significant traffic variability, and are open to model-level tradeoffs (batching/quantization) if quality holds.

Pain points we heard
- Per-inference costs spiking during bursts; hard to forecast monthly spend given bursty traffic and per-request endpoints.
- Current caching is per-session in-app, limited reuse of KV cache across users.
- Latency SLOs: need 95th < 300ms for interactive product; any multi-second tails break UX.
- Concern about quality regressions from aggressive quantization.

Current stack (as described)
- Model: in-house fine-tuned Llama2-70B variants served on managed endpoints (cloud vendor).
- Traffic: mix of short chat messages and multimodal prompts; monthly token volume ~150M, peak qps ~220.
- Ops: infra team runs autoscaling; ML team holds model variants; limited telemetry for per-route token distribution.

Success criteria you mentioned
- Cut per-inference unit cost by ~30–50% without >5% degradation in quality metrics (internal eval).
- Keep interactive latency within 300ms p95.
- Preserve easy rollbacks and traceability for regulated customers.

What Redwood can help with (summary)
- Quantization experiments (4-bit and 8-bit) with side-by-side evals and quality delta monitoring.
- Workload-aware batching + persistent KV cache to reduce repeated compute for similar prefixes.
- Cost model template (attached) to map token economics across model variants and batch sizes.
- Controlled pilot: we can run a dedicated pilot environment to measure real traffic post-integration.

Immediate next steps (proposed)
1) You share a 72-hour sample of prompt logs + traffic shape (anonymized) — this will let us recommend batch profiles and caching keys.
2) We’ll run an initial cost projection using the attached template and propose 2 pilot configs (conservative, aggressive).
3) Schedule a 60-minute technical deep dive with your infra + ML engineer next week to review network, telemetry hooks, and rollout plan.

I attached the cost-model template and a brief network-diagram stub describing our recommended telemetry hooks. Proposed time for deep dive: Apr 27 or Apr 29 (I included a cal link in the follow-up).

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
monica@redwood.inference
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: streamline-cost-modeling-template.xlsx (stub), streamline-network-diagram.png (stub)

Date: 2026-04-20T17:13:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: StreamlineAI cost & performance discovery — next steps

Thanks Monica — this is exactly the right summary. A few clarifications and confirmations: 
- We can provide a 72-hour anonymized prompt log (will scrub PII/PHI).
- We are open to trying 4-bit quantized variants in a canary for non-critical users. Concern: our internal quality metric is user-utterance acceptance rate; we need <5% delta.
- Network diagram attached on our side as well (we’ll share in the Drive link).

Can we book the technical deep dive on Apr 27 at 14:00 PT? Tom (ops) and our ML infra engineer Priya will join — Priya’s email is priya@streamlineai.com. Also, before the deep dive, could you confirm what telemetry hooks you need (token-level, per-route latency, cache hit rate)?

Alicia Gomez
Head of Machine Learning | StreamlineAI

Subject: Internal: StreamlineAI — quantization openness and pilot ask

Quick internal note after Alicia’s reply:
- They’ll share logs (anonymized) — good.
- They explicitly said they’re willing to canary 4-bit for non-critical users, but quality tolerance is tight (<5% acceptance delta).
- Key risk: their latency SLO and peak qps mean we must validate batching does not increase p95 above 300ms.

Proposed internal approach:
1) Aditya — can you prepare a quick benchmarking matrix: 70B fine-tuned baseline vs 8-bit vs 4-bit for our runtime with tokens-per-request distribution (I’ll send sample logs when available). Include p95 and throughput numbers.
2) Rishi — remind legal to prepare a short pilot MSA addendum that allows controlled canarying and telemetry access for 30 days.
3) I’ll draft a short success-metric spreadsheet (aligned with their acceptance rate + cost reduction targets) and push to the Drive link.

Monica
AE — Redwood Inference
